 PHOENIX, Ariz. (KVOA)  -- A college basketball player is taking his fight for athletic eligibility to court in Arizona.
 According to court filings, Clemson-transfer RJ Godfrey is scheduled to appear in court on Tuesday, Nov. 17, to take on the Arizona Board of Regents.
 The legal action marks Godfrey's third attempt this season to secure eligibility as a fifth-year player. He previously faced legal roadblocks during similar court challenges in Texas and Georgia.
 Under current rules in the United States, college athletes must take classes to play basketball. In contrast, European players normally only have to sign a contract with a professional club to play high-level basketball on their home continent.
